name: Ste. Anne de Detroit Catholic Church
history: French colonists under Antoine de la Mothe Cadillac founded Ste. Anne's on 26 July 1701, her feast day, two days after landing; the church was the first building of Fort Pontchartrain du Détroit. It is the second-oldest continuously operating Catholic parish in the United States. Several churches followed fires in 1703 and 1805. The present church was built in 1886-87, and Pope Francis named it a basilica in 2020.
arch: A red-brick Gothic Revival church with twin spires, facing a tree-lined brick plaza near the Ambassador Bridge.
features: The oldest surviving records begin on 2 February 1704 with the baptism of Cadillac's child.
Father Richard, who brought Detroit's first printing press and started The Observer newspaper, is buried under the altar.

look.d: They rise near the Ambassador Bridge to Canada.
The parish is older than the city of Detroit itself.

fun: The parish is as old as Detroit: the church was the fort's first building.
journal: 1701, French Detroit. The parish older than the city, under red-brick spires.
